subject: Air-gapped egress acceptance & cert handoff for AcmeNet private deployment
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Desai <priya@acmenet.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Air-gapped egress acceptance & cert handoff for AcmeNet private deployment

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the on-site yesterday. Per our acceptance checklist, we need a short packet of evidence to sign off the private deploy (control plane in Redwood-managed VPC, data plane in AcmeNet colo with air-gap to public internet):

- Confirmed egress fingerprint: one static NAT IP or documented egress appliance from your side.
- End-to-end TLS chain for the customer-facing model endpoint (signed cert + chain).
- Control plane connectivity proofs (outbound only, over allowed port/host) including timestamps and traceroutes.
- Result of the prefix/KV cache smoke tests and latency samples (sample windows attached as a CSV).

I attached the acceptance checklist we use (handoff-checklist.md) and a template for the egress test results. Can you provide the artifacts listed above by EOD PST so we can complete the internal compliance readout?

Technical notes: we will require the signed certificate to include the full chain (leaf+intermediate+root) in PEM form, and a thumbprint (SHA256) that we can validate against the CSR we generated. For egress, if you are using a pool that does SNAT, we need a stable mapping for at least 7 days post-cutover (or a documented failover mapping).

If there are any procurement or legal holds, loop them to the thread — otherwise cc'ing Jordan and Kim for ops/PKI validation.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Product Security Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: handoff-checklist.md (text), egress-test-results.pdf (stub)

From: Priya Desai <priya@acmenet.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, EdgeOps Solutions <edgeops@consults.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Air-gapped egress acceptance & cert handoff for AcmeNet private deployment

Neha — thanks, this is helpful. Quick update and artifacts attached.

What we completed today (attached files):
- acme-egress-validation.csv — 30-minute sampling of outbound flows from the inference cluster showing SNAT IP 54.210.34.12 (sticky for the sampling window).
- signed-cert.pem — full PEM bundle (leaf + intermediate). Thumbprint: 3b:7a:9f:... (SHA256).
- zip of diagnostic traceroutes and tcpdump snippets (not attached here; available in Drive link).

Notes and open items:
- EdgeOps ran the smoke tests for prefix/KV caching; latency is within the expected band (median P50=28ms for in-region, P95=68ms). They included a short summary in the CSV.
- We do not expose egress IPs as a managed product; we operate an HA pair of NAT appliances with advertised failover mapping. The primary mapping for outbound to the public egress pool is the IP above. We can commit to a 7-day stable mapping after cutover, extended on request.
- Cert chain: attached file includes chain. We rotated the intermediate yesterday per rotation calendar. Let us know if you need the CSR history.

"On Fri, May 17, 2028 at 08:14 Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks again for the on-site yesterday. Per our acceptance checklist..."

We can provide additional logs if required; what's the best secure channel for larger pcap artifacts? We uploaded a Drive folder and will PM you the link in the hubspot record.

—Priya
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, AcmeNet

Attachments: acme-egress-validation.csv (CSV), signed-cert.pem (PEM)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Desai <priya@acmenet.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 13:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Air-gapped egress acceptance & cert handoff for AcmeNet private deployment

Thanks Priya — this looks good for the initial pass. A couple of clarifications from ops that will make the acceptance bullet-proof for our runbook and SOC evidence: 

1) Egress stability: can EdgeOps confirm the NAT appliance state transitions with timestamps for the HA pair? A single sampled sticky mapping is helpful, but the acceptance evidence we store requires a short event log showing no remap during the sample window (or documented failover event). If you can include a 24-hour NAT log snippet, that covers us.

2) Control plane connectivity proof: we need three outbound connection traces from our control plane to the customer endpoint (control-plane -> customer-prov endpoint) showing successful TLS handshake and certificate validation from our side. Please provide the traceroute+curl -v output (timestamps) for the three attempts. This ensures the data plane is not trying to reverse the trust boundary.

3) Cert validation: signed-cert.pem is good — can you also include the issuer chain thumbprints (SHA256) in a small text file so our PKI team can cross-check against the CSR? We also prefer a signed OCSP staple sample if your CA supports stapling — that helps our periodic revalidation checks.

Suggested formatting: put the NAT log snippet as nat-log-20280517.txt, the three control-plane traces as cp-trace-1.txt / cp-trace-2.txt / cp-trace-3.txt, and a cert-thumbprints.txt file. Drop everything into the Drive folder you created (the link below) and mark the HubSpot deal record so our Compliance reviewer can fetch it directly.

"On Fri, May 17, 2028 at 11:03 Priya Desai <priya@acmenet.com> wrote:
> Neha — thanks, this is helpful. Quick update and artifacts attached."

If you prefer, EdgeOps can SFTP a tarball to the secure intake host — call that out and we'll arrange.

—Jordan
Staff Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: none (inline guidance)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Desai <priya@acmenet.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Air-gapped egress acceptance & cert handoff for AcmeNet private deployment

Perfect — thanks everyone for the quick turnaround. Summary and next steps for the readout: 

- AcmeNet to upload: nat-log-20280517.txt, cp-trace-1.txt/2/3.txt, cert-thumbprints.txt, and the pcap bundle to the Drive folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_acme-vpc-evidence).
- EdgeOps to mark HubSpot deal ACME-2394 as "evidence provided" once uploaded (we'll pull automatically).
- Redwood PKI will validate thumbprints and OCSP staple; ops will validate NAT stability and traceroutes.
- Assuming no abnormalities, Neha will sign acceptance and transition the project to onboarding (tenant provisioning + SLA handoff).

Acceptance conditional: if NAT logs show a failover event during the 24-hour window, we'll need a short post-mortem and proposed hardening (either scheduled static mapping or BGP-advertised failover) before final sign-off.

Thanks again — target internal acceptance review 2028-05-18 10:00 PST. Kim / Jordan, please flag if you need the files sooner for validation.

Neha Kapoor
Sr. Product Security Manager | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198
